report.summary: Audit of gui_catalogue.py (partial): Provenance date validation too weak; uses regex that accepts invalid dates like '2026-13-40', contradicting docstring claim of mandatory checked field. No concurrency issues visible (I/O functions missing). No full verification of three-layer refusal guarantee (missing parse_entry). Other potential issues (duplicate entry names, prompt fencing) lie in unseen code.
risks: DATE VALIDATION: Provenance.__post_init__ uses _DATE_RE which matches any '0000-00-00' pattern, not valid ISO-8601 dates. Malformed dates (e.g., '2026-13-40') pass, despite doc claiming mandatory, checked field. Could corrupt downstream sorting/filtering.
UNAUDITED CODE: load_catalogue, parse_entry, render_for_prompt are not in slice; cannot verify docstring guarantees about three-layer refusal, atomicity, or prompt injection mitigation.
NAME UNIQUENESS: Catalogue.by_name returns first match; no duplicate detection visible. Could silently return wrong entry if duplicates exist.
todos: Strengthen Provenance date validation to reject invalid dates (e.g., use datetime.strptime).
Verify parse_entry properly quarantines bad entries; ensure Catalogue constructor rejects missing licences (already present).
Add duplicate name check during Catalogue construction or parsing.

handoff.suggestion: Provide full gui_catalogue.py to enable audit of file I/O (atomicity, concurrency), search/render functions, and the quarantine layer. The date validation bug is high priority because it undermines a 'mandatory checked' guarantee.
